notes: Credentials resolve from `beam login`; no eval should expect the skill to ask for an API key.
Build evals leave a DRAFT agent behind — run them against a non-production workspace.
Error-path evals (3-5) are read-only: they create nothing.

evals.name: linear-integration-blog-emailer
evals.prompt: Build me a Beam agent that takes a topic, writes a short blog post about it (around 400 words), and emails the finished post to me. I use Gmail.
evals.expected_output: A deployed Beam agent (draft, not published) with an entry node, a custom GPT node that writes the blog post using a proper ## Role/## Task/## Context/## Rules prompt, and a Gmail integration node whose subject/body are linked to the writer node's outputs. Before deploying, the skill asks exactly one clarifying question about the recipient address, shows a Mermaid diagram, and waits for the word `build`. It reports the agent as a draft and asks before publishing.

evals.name: condition-node-ticket-triage
evals.prompt: I need a Beam agent that triages support tickets. It should read the ticket text, classify it as billing, technical, or general, and then draft a reply tailored to whichever category it falls into.
evals.expected_output: A deployed Beam agent (draft) with a classifier node, a conditionNode (llm_based) that branches to three handlers, each branch edge carrying an explicit non-empty condition (including a written catch-all for the general case). Downstream reply nodes link to the classifier's output. A Mermaid diagram with a diamond condition node is shown for approval first. The reply nodes are terminal: the brief asked only for a draft, so the skill must NOT invent a send/email step.

evals.name: waiting-node-welcome-followup
evals.prompt: Can you create a Beam agent that sends a new customer a welcome email, then waits 2 days and sends a follow-up check-in email? Both emails go over Gmail.
evals.expected_output: A deployed Beam agent (draft) with two Gmail integration nodes and a waitingNode (time_based, 2 days) chained sequentially between them. The waiting node is not the entry node, has one outgoing edge, and the flow is entry -> write welcome -> send welcome -> wait -> write follow-up -> send follow-up.

evals.name: error-not-signed-in
evals.prompt: Build me a Beam agent that summarises my open support tickets each morning.
evals.setup: Run with BEAM_CONFIG_DIR pointing at an empty directory and BEAM_API_KEY unset, so `validate` exits 3 with code auth_error.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs `validate` first, sees the non-zero exit, and STOPS. It relays the `next` field — telling the user to run `beam login` in a terminal — and does not proceed to intake or design. It must NOT ask the user to paste an API key into the chat, and must not retry the same command unchanged.

evals.name: error-no-workspace-selected
evals.prompt: List my Beam agents and then build one that files expense reports.
evals.setup: Credentials present but no BEAM_WORKSPACE_ID set, so `validate` exits 2 with code validation_error.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops on the non-zero exit and helps the user choose a workspace with `beam workspace list <search>` then `beam workspace <id>`. It does not guess a workspace and does not continue to design.

evals.name: error-duplicate-objective
evals.prompt: Here is my spec, deploy it.
evals.setup: Provide a spec whose nodes share one `objective` string; `deploy --dry-run` exits 2 with 'Duplicate node objective values'.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains that integrations are matched to nodes by objective text, so duplicates would attach the tool to the wrong node. It gives each node a distinct objective and re-runs the dry run. It does not deploy the broken spec and does not silently change anything else.

evals.name: update-existing-agent-smallest-patch
evals.prompt: Change the tone of the reply node on my ticket triage agent to be more formal.
evals.setup: An existing deployed agent with a reply node.
evals.expected_output: The skill identifies the agent, runs `get-nodes` then `get-node`, shows the proposed change and waits for `build`, then applies the SMALLEST command that fits — `update-node-prompt` — rather than a full `deploy --agent-id` redeploy. It reports the result as a draft and asks before publishing.
